clue.text: Those who know of former spouse's impudent son

blocks.note: an ex is a former husband or wife
pert means cheeky or saucy
S is the standard abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Knowledgeable people have heard about a cheeky boy whose mother or father is divorced.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive on spouse's simply joins the pieces; experts are those in the know.
explanation.definitionFit: Specialists with deep understanding of a subject are people with real knowledge, so they are those who know.

clue.text: Consequently following new ensign up at first

indicators.note: something new is made afresh, so these letters are given a fresh order
at first points to the very start of the word before it, its opening letter

blocks.note: taken as written
the opening letter of up

explanation.surface: A newly commissioned naval officer is promoted, and something follows as a result.
explanation.definitionFit: Ensuing describes what comes after as a result, so it means coming next as a consequence.

clue.text: Devotion to a deity? Goodness!

blocks.note: first meaning: religious devoutness
second meaning: virtue, moral uprightness

explanation.walkthrough: Goodness! reads as an exclamation of surprise, but it is a plain noun for virtue here.
explanation.definitionFit: Being devout means worshipping fervently, and the quality is also treated as general virtue or holiness of character.

clue.text: Managed good English collection

blocks.note: to run a business is to manage it
G is the abbreviation for good
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Someone curated a fine set of English items.
explanation.definitionFit: A range is a set of products or items of a similar kind, offered or held together as a group.

clue.text: Device for security gets ten up

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the word is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: safety is security from harm
taken as written, then read backwards

explanation.surface: A security gadget ends up adding ten more.
explanation.walkthrough: Device for security reads as the whole definition, but for security is the first chunk of wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A safety net is a mesh or arrangement that catches people who fall, a contrivance or measure that protects.

clue.text: Boarding school bedroom is considered excellent to begin with for sleepy little creatures

indicators.note: what comes to begin with is the start of each word, so only opening letters count

blocks.note: a dorm is a shared bedroom at a boarding school
the opening letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A boarding-school dormitory gets high praise as a home for sleepy small animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Dormice are small rodents famous for long hibernation, like the drowsy one at the Mad Hatter's tea party.

clue.text: Originally, did Ed choose one room's colours and furnishings?

indicators.note: originally points to what each word has at its origin, its opening letter

blocks.note: the opening letters of these five words

explanation.surface: Was it Ed who picked the paint and furniture for a room?
explanation.definitionFit: Decor is the style of a room's interior, its paint, furniture and ornaments taken together.

clue.text: Dieter ran badly and was taught new ways

indicators.note: done badly means done wrongly, so the letters come out in the wrong order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A slimmer had a poor run and so went back for coaching.
explanation.definitionFit: To be retrained is to receive fresh instruction, learning different skills or methods than before.

clue.text: Images in one study she's beginning

indicators.note: a word's beginning is its opening letter only

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
to con is an old word for to study or learn by heart
the opening letter of she's

explanation.surface: A woman starts looking at pictures in her den.
explanation.walkthrough: Study looks like a room but is the verb: to con a text is to pore over it.
explanation.definitionFit: Icons are pictures, especially religious paintings, or small symbols on a screen, so they are images.

clue.text: Perhaps see it as being most comfortable

indicators.note: perhaps signals a possible version, so the letters may be arranged otherwise

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone may regard something as the cosiest option.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy can mean relaxed and at ease, so the superlative describes the greatest comfort available.

clue.text: Sean said to have been been sheared

indicators.note: said means spoken, so we use how the name is pronounced, not its spelling

blocks.note: the name pronounced in a non-rhotic British accent

explanation.surface: Sean apparently had his hair cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated been is a typo in the source. In British speech the r is silent, so the name and the answer rhyme exactly.
explanation.definitionFit: Shorn is the past participle of shear, meaning cut off wool or hair, so it equals sheared.

clue.text: Playful aspect of promissory notes

blocks.note: a facet is one side or aspect of something
an IOU is a written promise to pay a debt

explanation.surface: Someone describes the light-hearted side of written debts.
explanation.definitionFit: A facetious remark is flippant and jokey, treating serious things lightly, so it is playful.

clue.text: Examiner to check gold

blocks.note: to inspect is to check closely
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: An assayer is sent to verify some gold.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is gold in heraldry, from French.
explanation.definitionFit: An inspector is an official who looks over premises, work or documents to judge their standard.

clue.text: Way to get married in church? I'll say!

definitions.text: Way to get married in church

indicators.note: say asks us to speak the phrase, using its sound rather than its spelling

blocks.note: the contraction of I will pronounced

explanation.surface: An excited reply to a question about how to wed in church.
explanation.walkthrough: I'll say! looks like an exclamation of agreement; it is a sound cue on the contraction before it.
explanation.definitionFit: The bride walks down the central passage of a church to her wedding, so it is the route to the altar.

clue.text: Impressive kind of force altered rate  …

indicators.note: altered means changed, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: g-force is measured in units of gravity, g
taken as written

explanation.surface: A strong force has changed the speed of something, leading into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis ties this clue to 15 across for the surface only; the wordplay is complete here.
explanation.definitionFit: Great describes something remarkable in size, ability or importance, which makes it impressive.

clue.text: Fearful about term at university for Lou's son

indicators.note: about means around in different directions, so the word is jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written, then jumbled
U is the abbreviation for university
the name taken as written
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A parent is anxious about their son's first term at college.
explanation.definitionFit: Tremulous means trembling or timid, the shaky manner of someone nervous or afraid.

clue.text: …  the result was a foregone conclusion

definitions.text: the result was a foregone conclusion

blocks.clueFragment: the result was a foregone conclusion
blocks.note: surface reading: following on from 13, a contest whose outcome was obvious before it began

blocks.clueFragment: the result was a foregone conclusion
blocks.note: setter's reading: a phrase for a match so one-sided that it hardly counted as a match

explanation.surface: After a great force was applied, the outcome was never in doubt.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this to 13 across for the surface; read alone, the phrase describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a competition so unequal that one side was certain to win from the start.

clue.text: My clanger about the vicar?

indicators.note: about means turned around every which way, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to a social blunder concerning the local priest.
explanation.walkthrough: A clanger is British slang for an embarrassing mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: A vicar is a parish priest in the Church of England, one example of an ordained minister.

clue.text: Lie mole made up to National Trust to get cream

indicators.note: something made up is invented or put together afresh, so the letters are reassembled

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
NT is the abbreviation for the National Trust, the British heritage charity

explanation.surface: A burrowing animal is told to lie down so the heritage body can get some ointment.
explanation.definitionFit: An emollient is a soothing preparation that softens the skin, such as a lotion or moisturiser.

clue.text: He has tune playing to remove protective covering

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are played with and rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A musician keeps a melody going while taking an instrument out of its case.
explanation.definitionFit: To unsheathe a sword or knife is to draw it out of the scabbard that guards its blade.

clue.text: Defenceless, but United Nations are equipped and ready

blocks.note: UN is the abbreviation for the United Nations
armed means equipped with weapons and prepared

explanation.surface: A paradox: someone is helpless though the peacekeepers stand by fully kitted out.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sets the answer against its own parts: weaponless, yet built from a word meaning carrying weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: Unarmed means without weapons, and so unable to fight back or protect oneself.

clue.text: Run into toy — that's funny!

indicators.note: going into something means being placed inside it

blocks.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for a run
a doll is a child's toy

explanation.surface: A child bumps into a plaything and finds it amusing.
explanation.definitionFit: Droll means quaintly amusing or wryly humorous, so the exclamation says something is comic.

clue.text: The French and English draw back to the sheltered side

indicators.note: drawing back means going in the opposite direction, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: le is French for the
E is the abbreviation for English
taken as written, then turned round

explanation.surface: The French and the English retreat behind cover.
explanation.walkthrough: Draw back reads as one verb, retreat, but back is a separate signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeward is the side away from the wind, so it is the side protected from the weather.

clue.text: Wrong idea: turn and say goodbye in Paris

indicators.note: wrong means not correct, so the letters are in a mistaken order

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
a U-turn, so U stands for a turn

explanation.surface: Realising a plan is mistaken, someone turns round and bids farewell in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu is the French word for farewell, used when parting for a long time.

clue.text: Condition in old city quarter

blocks.note: taken as written
Ur is the ancient Sumerian city
E for east, one of the four compass quarters

explanation.surface: Someone describes the state of a historic district of a town.
explanation.walkthrough: Condition looks like a noun meaning state, but it is a verb. Ur and compass points are crossword staples.
explanation.definitionFit: To inure someone is to accustom them to hardship until they no longer feel it, training their responses.

clue.text: Pretty lady holding a gun, but it's just a game

indicators.note: holding means keeping something inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: a belle is a beautiful woman
taken as written
gat is old American slang for a pistol

explanation.surface: A beautiful woman brandishes a pistol, but it's only play-acting.
explanation.walkthrough: Bagatelle is a table game of balls and pins, and the word also means a trifle, which suits just.
explanation.definitionFit: Bagatelle is a pub and parlour pastime where balls are struck into holes on a board, ancestor of pinball.

clue.text: Bow liberal accepted to amalgamate

indicators.note: something accepted is taken in, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: to bow is to bend over
L is the abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: A politician bows and agrees to a merger.
explanation.definitionFit: To blend things is to mix them so they combine into one, the same as merging them.

clue.text: Empty threat about our broadcast for fish

indicators.note: an empty word has had its inside removed, leaving just the outer letters
broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are strewn about
about means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

blocks.note: the first and last letters of threat
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: An idle threat goes out on the airwaves about catching fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A trout is a freshwater fish of the salmon family, prized by anglers and cooks.

clue.text: Mum went around clinging to gold, alone in a burial chamber

indicators.note: going around something means encircling it, so the rest sits inside

blocks.note: taken as written, then split around the rest
Au is the chemical symbol for gold
sole means single or alone

explanation.surface: A mother clutches her gold, alone in a tomb.
explanation.definitionFit: A mausoleum is a grand stone building housing a tomb or tombs, a chamber for the dead.

clue.text: Foreign game, first love has the last word

indicators.note: something foreign is strange and unfamiliar, so the letters appear in an unfamiliar order

blocks.note: love is zero, the letter O, placed first
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: In an overseas match, the leading sweetheart gets the final say.
explanation.walkthrough: Love means nil in tennis, hence O. The first is an instruction to place the O at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the final letter of the Greek alphabet, so figuratively the end or final word of something.

clue.text: Medic had different seeds to be prepared

indicators.note: different means changed from the original, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctor had a new variety of seeds ready for planting.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressed food, like a salad or a carcass, has been made ready for cooking or eating.

clue.text: Recorded music?

blocks.note: surface reading: music captured on tape or disc
setter's reading: music written down on paper as symbols on a stave

explanation.walkthrough: Recorded suggests a studio; the question mark hints that it means written down instead.
explanation.definitionFit: To notate music is to write it in musical notation, so a score set down on paper has been put on record.
